modules.title: Introduction to Ancient Greek
modules.description: Functional reading competence in Ancient Greek — enough to work through texts on Perseus with grammar and lexicon support. Attic Greek through Section 1, Koine transition in Section 2.

references.title: A Greek Grammar for Colleges (Smyth)
references.description: Comprehensive Attic Greek reference grammar (Smyth, 1920). Also available digitally on Perseus.

references.title: Liddell-Scott-Jones Greek-English Lexicon (Online)
references.description: The standard Ancient Greek lexicon, fully searchable on Perseus Digital Library

references.title: Perseus Digital Library — Greek & Roman Collection (Online)
references.description: Full-text Greek and Roman works with morphological analysis, interlinear glosses, and linked lexicon entries

references.title: Greek in a Nutshell
references.description: Compact Ancient Greek grammar for beginners (Strong, 1903)

references.title: Sappho: Memoir, Text, Selected Renderings
references.description: Greek text of Sappho's fragments with English translations (Wharton, 1885)

references.title: Early Greek Philosophy
references.description: Source fragments of the Pre-Socratic philosophers with commentary (Burnet, 1892)

chapters.title: Orienting to the Tools — Smyth, Perseus, and the LSJ
The Case System and the Article
Verbs: Tense, Mood, and the Participle
Reading Attic Prose and Verse — Capstone

modules.title: Modern Algebra
modules.description: From variables and unknowns through calculus-readiness — following the historical development of algebraic thinking from Diophantus through Euler. The module traces the transition from geometric to algebraic reasoning, develops symbolic notation alongside the primary texts, and introduces trigonometry and logarithms as they arise from the physics.

chapters.title: Completing the Square and Equation Types
Mathematical Induction and the Binomial Coefficients

modules.title: Calculus
modules.description: From the problems that demanded calculus through vector calculus — following Newton and Leibniz through Maxwell. The module retraces Archimedes and Fermat with algebraic tools, develops single-variable calculus alongside the Principia, then extends to multivariable and vector calculus as demanded by electrodynamics.

chapters.title: Pre-Calculus Synthesis — Fermat, Archimedes, and the Problems that Demanded Calculus
The Integral and the Fundamental Theorem
Multivariable Calculus — Partial Derivatives and Multiple Integrals

modules.title: Foundations of Modern Mathematics
modules.description: A survey of the 19th-century mathematical explosion and the foundations crisis — from complex numbers and rigorous analysis through set theory and non-Euclidean geometry to formal logic and Gödel's incompleteness. Like the Programming Languages module, this is a survey: each chapter opens a door to an area of modern mathematics, building reading competence rather than deep mastery.

chapters.title: Complex Numbers and the Algebraic Closure
The Real Numbers and Dedekind Cuts
Riemann and the Generalization of Space
Formal Logic and the Foundations Crisis

modules.title: Computation from First Principles
modules.description: The physical story of computation — from Boolean algebra and logic gates through machine architecture to assembly language. Exercises are pen-and-paper or web-simulator based; hands-on electrical work lives in a separate lab supplement.

chapters.title: Boolean Algebra and the Algebra of Logic
Combinational Logic — From Gates to Arithmetic
Sequential Logic — Memory, State, and Clocks
Machine Architecture — The Von Neumann Model
Assembly Language — Writing for the Machine
From Turing Machines to Physical Computers — Capstone

modules.title: Programming Languages and Paradigms
modules.description: A survey of programming paradigms through their foundational texts — from lambda calculus and LISP through C and structured programming to type theory and formal verification. Reading competence across paradigms, not deep fluency in any one language.

chapters.title: Types, Proofs, and the Curry-Howard Correspondence

modules.title: Data Structures, Algorithms, and Software Engineering in C++
modules.description: The capstone module of the Enchiridion curriculum. Deep proficiency in C++ through data structures, algorithms, and software engineering — culminating in Stepanov and McJones's Elements of Programming. Stroustrup's The C++ Programming Language serves as the comprehensive reference.

chapters.title: C++ Foundations — Types and the Memory Model
C++ Foundations — RAII and the Standard Library
Recursion, Dynamic Programming, and Greedy Strategies
